newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Second group of Chinese troops to enter Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Second group of Chinese troops to enter Hong Kong.

text.p: A second contingent of troops from China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) will arrive in Hong Kong next week to help set up the PLA garrison that will take over when Britain withdraws, the British army said on Wednesday.

The arrival of 66 PLA troops on Monday will bring to 106 the total number of PLA soldiers stationed in the British colony as it prepares for its midnight June 30 return to China, the army said. The first 40 advance party troops arrived on April 21.

"The purpose is to act as an advance party, to take over barracks, set up administrative arrangements. It's a standard administrative event," British army spokeswoman Captain Sarah Wood told Reuters. A further 90 PLA troops would arrive in Hong Kong on May 30 to set up barracks, she said.

Next Mondays' contingent would drive into Hong Kong in 13 military vehicles through the Lok Ma Chau land border post, where their comrades came in three weeks ago. A small military liaison party would greet them and escort them to barracks, Wood said.
China is resuming sovereignty over Hong Kong after 156 years of British rule there, and the PLA will be responsible for its defence after the British garrison, now very small, withdraws.
China is expected eventually to station up to 10,000 troops in Hong Kong, the level reached by Britain at its peak.
